title: Unmatched: Delivery promise and fulfillment network panel
title_note: Not yet matched to an agenda session. Panel with a DoorDash executive (mentions launching drone delivery with Lowe's in Charlotte) and the CEO of a direct-to-consumer mattress brand owned by a manufacturer, plus a moderator.
transcript_note: The recording starts partway through the session. Song lyrics picked up after the session ended were removed.
takeaways: Retailers already stock the best SKUs for their market, so DoorDash puts items in its own fulfilment nodes mainly for late-night demand or fast movers that stores struggle to keep in stock.
The mattress brand plans capacity from 30-day trailing order concentration and saturates target markets (e.g. Phoenix); its oversized boxes make shipping costly, so pricing is built around that.
Automate only once a process is proven and tied to a real customer problem; go high-touch first to learn where the pain is. DoorDash has launched drone delivery with Lowe's in Charlotte.
Align marketing promises with actual operations: DoorDash sets advertised delivery times each quarter from real delivery data; the mattress brand uses NPS as its shared north star.
Advice: stop copying competitors, and stop communicating with customers the way you used to.
